subject: Capacity pacing and surge-smoothing for CloudWave Dedicated
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@cloudwave.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudWave Sales Ops <sales+ops@cloudwave.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity pacing and surge-smoothing for CloudWave Dedicated

Hi Ben / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're excited to move forward with a Dedicated deployment, but before we sign we need clarity on how Redwood would handle predictable daily peaks plus a few unpredictable, high-variance burst windows tied to our marketing promotions.

High-level:
- Baseline steady state: ~60 GPU-hours / hour equivalent across inference fleet (token-heavy chat).
- Predictable peaks: +40% for 2–3 hours PDT, usually 3x per week.
- Promotion bursts: spikes up to 4–6x baseline for ~30–90 minutes, irregular schedule but mostly within a two-hour promo window.

What we need from you:
1) Suggested dedicated sizing to meet our SLA (99.9% availability, 200ms median token latency for interactive flows).
2) Recommended autoscaling & burst policy for Dedicated customers — how will headroom, shoulder pools, and ephemeral burst capacity work?
3) How preemption/eviction works if you use ephemeral or shared pools during bursts.
4) A rough capex/opex delta vs committing more reserve capacity.

I attached a simple traffic model (cloudwave_capacity_model.xlsx) — it's high level but should help. Can we get a written proposal before Monday? If it helps, happy to set a short call to walk through the numbers.

Cheers,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform, CloudWave AI

Attachment: cloudwave_capacity_model.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@cloudwave.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity pacing and surge-smoothing for CloudWave Dedicated

Liam — thanks for the model and the clear ask. Quick notes and we'll follow up with a short technical proposal + cost delta by EOD Monday.

Short answers up front:
- Sizing: we'll propose a recommended reserved pool sized for your 99.9% SLA for baseline + predictable peaks; ephemeral burst capacity for short promotions.
- Autoscale & policy: recommend a two-tier approach (reserved slab + ephemeral shoulder pool + transient burst credits) with configurable cooldowns and enforced max burst multiplier.
- Preemption: ephemeral instances are preemptible; we provide graceful eviction (drain with KV cache handoff) and fallback routing to lower-cost models if capacity is constrained.

Action items for us: Karthik and Soojin will draft the capacity plan (numbers + operational runbook). Marissa — I'll loop you in for commercial delta and any accelerated SOW options.

Would you be available for a 30-min call Monday 9:30–11am PDT or Tuesday 11am PDT?

-Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 23 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: CloudWave sizing & surge-smoothing proposal (technical)

Ben / Soojin — first pass draft, technical considerations and numbers based on the spreadsheet Liam sent. Leaving enough detail so the commercial team can map costs.

Assumptions pulled from model:
- Baseline compute (steady state): equivalently 60 GPU-hours / hr -> recommend base reserved slab = 64 A100-equivalent GPUs (rounded to slab sizing) to meet median latency SLOs.
- Predictable peaks: +40% -> operational buffer: reserve an additional 30% of slab as "shoulder pool" in the same region (us-west) that can be ramped within 5–10 min.
- Promotion bursts: spikes up to 4–6x baseline for 30–90 mins. We recommend handling these via ephemeral burst capacity with the following guardrails:
  - Max burst multiplier: 5x baseline per customer (configurable upward by mutual agreement).
  - Burst credits: purchaseable burst credits that reduce per-token price for agreed burst minutes.
  - Burst prewarming: customers can schedule promoter windows to prewarm KV-cache and reduce cold-starts (we expose a simple API to prewarm model shards).

Autoscale policy (recommended defaults):
- Scale unit: GPU/node pool.
- Cooldown: 120s for upward scaling, 600s for downward (to avoid oscillation during campaign spikes).
- Aggressive-add strategy: when we detect >80% CPU/GPU util sustained for 90s AND 95th-token-latency breaches, trigger instant +15% slab allocation (to a max of shoulder pool).
- Burst allocation: ephemeral pool provisions from a shared burst cluster with 2-minute boot path; allow 30s for prewarming hooks if scheduled.
- Eviction strategy: LRU-like selection for ephemeral pods; 60s drain window to flush KV cache. In-flight requests will be re-routed to reserved slab or a quantized variant model if needed.

Operational concerns / runbook items:
- Alerting on burst >3x baseline for >15min -> paging to SRE + Customer Ops.
- SLA carve-outs: bursts beyond contracted credits may see best-effort latency and cost surcharges.
- Telemetry: token-level latency, per-route token counts, and headroom metrics exposed in Console.

Numbers (rough cost delta):
- Full reserved for 5x baseline: ~3.8x higher monthly commit vs our recommended slab + burst credits.
- Slab + shoulder + 1k burst credits / month: ~1.35x commit, with predictable marginal costs when credits used.

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_template.pdf (template for SOW + service terms) attached to help map commercial language to these technical controls.

If this looks good I can convert to a short writeup for the commercial team and include specific GPU SKU counts (we should pick target SKUs after price discussion).

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_dedicated_template.pdf (PDF, 95KB)
From: Priya Menon <priya.m@cloudwave.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam@cloudwave.ai>, CloudWave Sales Ops <sales+ops@cloudwave.ai>
Date: Sun, 24 Jun 2028 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity pacing and surge-smoothing for CloudWave Dedicated

Ben / Karthik — thanks for the quick turnaround and the draft. A few clarifications from procurement/ops perspective: 

1) We prefer a contracted committed slab that covers baseline + predictable peaks (your 64 GPUs + 30% shoulder makes sense) and then buy burst credits for marketing windows. Can you produce an example MOP (mutual action plan) showing procurement milestones, dates for ramp, and DocuSign-ready SOW language?

2) Regional requirement: us-west preferred, with optional failover to us-east. Any cross-region failover should not count against burst credits (we only want credits applied to us-west bursts).

3) Compliance: we'll need audit logs and key management proof (KMS) to be included in the SOW; SOC2 plus breach notification SLA spelled out.

Also — please confirm eviction behaviour: if an ephemeral node is preempted mid-request, will Redwood attempt to retry the request on reserved slab or return an error to caller? We need deterministic client behaviour for our SDK.

We can do the call Monday 9:30 PDT to finalize the MOP if that works.

Best,
Priya
Priya Menon
Head of Procurement, CloudWave AI

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Menon <priya.m@cloudwave.ai>, Liam O'Connor <liam@cloudwave.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 24 Jun 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity pacing and surge-smoothing for CloudWave Dedicated

Priya / Liam — thanks, outlining next steps and answers below so we have everything in writing before the call Monday 9:30 PDT.

Agreed items:
- Reserved slab: 64 GPUs in us-west, with an allocated shoulder pool of 19 GPUs (30% of slab) that can be ramped within 5–10 minutes.
- Burst credits: CloudWave will purchase an initial 1,000 burst-credit minutes at signup (applies to us-west only). Additional credits can be purchased or auto-top up with approval.
- Max burst multiplier: default 5x baseline. Any permanent increase requires amendment to SOW.
- Eviction behaviour: ephemeral nodes are preemptible. If an ephemeral node is interrupted mid-request Redwood will attempt a single retry on reserved slab (best-effort). If retry would violate token latency SLA we will return an error; SDK guidance will include idempotency and client-side retry bindings. We will document exact retry semantics in the SOW appendix.
- Compliance & audit: we'll include KMS integration options and SOC2 attestation clauses in the SOW; breach-notification SLA will be 72 hours by default (can be tightened under enterprise terms).

Action items (owners & dates):
- Ben: build the MOP + DocuSign-ready SOW draft (using redwood_dedicated_template.pdf) and send by Mon 08:00 PDT.
- Karthik: finalize GPU SKU mapping and exact headroom counts for reserved slab vs shoulder pool by Mon 08:00 PDT.
- Marissa: pricing options for slab-only vs slab+burst-credits and an example billing cadence (monthly invoice + usage invoice).
- Priya: confirm internal procurement dates and sign-off owners on Monday call.

We'll attach the MOP and SOW drafts in the Monday follow-up. Thanks — talk Monday at 9:30.

Best,

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
